In this segment on Marvelous Designer, I will introduce a style reminiscent of the 20th century and how to wear a more casual set of sportswear. To put it simply, I will demonstrate how to use different tools in our software to create various clothing pieces. I noticed on Weibo that many people are unsure how to work with Marvelous Designer, particularly regarding clothing cladding and folding techniques for heavier layers. Today, I am here to introduce these features to you. Let’s get started! ## Overview of Marvelous Designer There are several ways to create clothes in Marvelous Designer. For instance, when designing tight-fitting garments, we typically import a model from Marvelous Designer and extract the pattern from it. The top of the garment we’ve just created is in a tight state, making manual pattern drawing inconvenient. Hence, I prefer to use the 3D modeling virtual model tool to sketch lines on the virtual model. It may appear a bit monotonous, so let's pause for a moment. I will play some background music while we proceed. ### Using Marvelous Designer 11 What you see now is Marvelous Designer 11. Here we have some repetitive operations. I select the area on the virtual model. In previous versions of Marvelous Designer, it was also possible to draw directly on the virtual model. However, some of my friends may not be aware of this feature in the 3D modeling tool. After finishing the selection area, we can use the extract pattern function to select the areas we've drawn. We press the Enter key, and it will automatically extract the pattern. Once extracted, we will manually align them in the 2D window and position them correctly. ## Aligning Patterns Due to my compulsive nature, I prefer to arrange items neatly in a flat position, so I will realign them again in the 2D window. Next, we will create lines between these pincers. After creating a line, we press the Control key and simulate to see that this top will soon have a line. Given that this is a compact pattern, we need to reduce its surface diameter. There is a layer of air around the virtual model to prevent collision between the pattern and the model. Since our virtual model has a relatively small grid and the default particle diameter of the pattern is 20, this particle diameter is relatively large. If the pattern is too close to the body, it may become unstable and penetrate. ### Adjusting Particle Diameter Therefore, when each virtual model is inserted, its default particle diameter is set to 20. To protect the pattern, the default surface diameter of the virtual model is 3. When making tight clothes, we need to reduce the surface diameter. I will set the particle diameter to 10. The pattern we extract from the virtual model is similar to the UV extraction process, so the extracted pattern cannot be as flat as we manually create. However, we can apply some other processing to modify this pattern. ## Physical Properties of the Pattern Now, let's look at the physical properties of the pattern, including fineness, strength, and angles of rotation. In the latest version of Marvelous Designer, one of the new features includes the ability to change the left and right angles of rotation. The function for automatic layout of the pattern has not yet been manually displayed. After adjusting the fineness, strength, and angles of rotation, the benefit of this adjustment is that the fabric will become easier to stretch. In simple terms, it will not form irregular wrinkles. If the pattern is too tight and the fabric is not easy to stretch, wrinkles will easily occur. Conversely, by reducing these physical properties, the dress becomes flexible, making it less prone to wrinkles. Additionally, it enhances the appearance of the chest area, rendering wrinkles less obvious. ### Observing and Adjusting the Dress Let’s observe this dress. After reviewing, we will see that the length of this pattern is incorrect. To facilitate adjustments, we first delete the curve points on these two lines. Curve points can significantly affect the side line effect. We will convert these two lines into straight lines and match their lengths. On the side, you will notice that its wrinkles disappear and the surface becomes smooth. Wrinkles often occur due to differing lengths on either side, so matching the length will smooth out the wrinkles. ## Addressing Wrinkles In the comments, someone mentioned the pinch function. I'm not sure if you refer to the pinch function in carving. The pinch function in carving is used to refine wrinkles. Let’s identify any issues with this dress. It has very uneven wrinkles. In a previous video, I introduced that to remove this wrinkle, we can use the pinch function, similar to XiaoYunDouYang, to press it, causing it to shrink. However, the downside is that the pinch function automatically sets the wrinkles between the lines to flatten. ### Using Shen In our discussion, "Shen" refers to a piece of cloth we dig out, creating a small triangle and sewing the two sides together for an even finish. However, adding Shen can be a challenging operation. The most difficult operation is to create a false stitch. We select this position and connect these two points. This is why it is called false sewing—two points are sewn together. When these two points connect, we examine the line carefully, and it appears very smooth. ## Adjusting the Curve We have more material between these two points. We use the plus point tool to add a straight point near the midpoint of these points, right-click it to create a triangular area. After digging this area, we can use the editor sewing tool to delete the false stitch we used as a reference. After deletion, you will see that this curve is indeed smoother than before. If we adjust it further, it still protrudes slightly, so we will enlarge this gap a bit. After reducing it, let’s examine this clothing piece. It appears very smooth on the side, with minimal protrusions, indicating that our adjustments have been successful. ## Final Adjustments Now, we will address the folds in front of the chest. My ideal form for the chest area is to have it smooth and tightly fitted without any folds. If you utilize tools effectively, I have shown you before how to reduce protrusions, achieving a smooth appearance. This tool smudges without directly flattening the protruding parts. The key is to reduce the grid; this is what we refer to as the “tool.” If you shrink this grid, the shape will deform, as this grid shrinks inward. ### Sewing Techniques Next, we can sew a few points together using a fake needle to see if we can dig away this area, making it flat. Most wrinkles are formed due to excessive fabric, so if the fabric is tight without any excess, it generally won’t wrinkle. ## Repeating Operations I keep repeating these operations to add a fake needle. When you increase the bending intensity, the fabric becomes less prone to bending, allowing the wrinkle to connect seamlessly into a curve. ### Adjustments in 3D Window Let's take a close look. When adjusting wrinkles, I add a straight line on both sides because if a curve is continuous and modified, it will affect the entire curve. Therefore, when adjusting curves, if you identify an ideal curve, add a breakpoint to adjust the lower part separately or focus on adjusting the primary line. ## Managing Protrusions I still find that the front of the chest has some protruding areas.
